top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a mature, independently reproduced instrument achievement: the magic-wavelength lattice removes first-order shifts, and several laboratories (RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE, NPL) have reached the 10^-18 level, with calibration and systematics under control. The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye is clean and every other member supports it, so it fits the statutes without compromise. Aberration-corrected electron microscopy is a real detector and instrument advance and ranks second, but it has a single supporter and its allocation is less settled. No award is the weakest option when a decisive, confirmed achievement is available.
